finding: INV-4 still violated for one of the three URLs the DESIGN names as reported defects. `capability_probe_url(HuggingFace, repo_url)` ignores `repo_url` entirely and probes the fixed `hf_api_base()/api/models?limit=1`, so ANY row whose host is huggingface.co — including the reported `https://huggingface.co/custom` — is confirmed `healthy` on the strength of huggingface.co's own catalogue, not that URL's capability. It cannot serve models: `GitService::build_repository_url` (src-app/server/src/utils/git/service.rs:699) builds the HF clone as `{url}/{path}`, i.e. `https://huggingface.co/custom/org/model`, which is not a repository. The author recognised this exact class for GitHub and added `is_clonable_github_origin` (utils.rs:355) so `api.github.com` degrades to `unverified`; the symmetric HF origin/path guard was never written. Reachability of a DIFFERENT url is being reported as this url's confirmed capability.

Test that CERTIFIES the unfixed defect above. `a_hugging_face_host_is_probed_against_the_hugging_face_listing_surface` creates a repository at `https://huggingface.co/org-<uuid>` — an arbitrary, non-existent HF path with the same shape as the reported `huggingface.co/custom` — and its positive-control half asserts `good_result["status"] == "healthy"` and `good_status == "healthy"` (lines 401-414). The paired unit test `capability_url_targets_the_kinds_listing_surface` (src-app/server/src/modules/llm_repository/utils.rs:983) asserts literally `capability_probe_url(HuggingFace, "https://huggingface.co/custom") == "https://huggingface.co/api/models?limit=1"`, pinning the reported URL to the confirming path. Both tests would go RED if INV-4 were actually satisfied for this input, so they lock the defect in.

INV-4 ('a repository whose capability could not be confirmed is never auto-disabled') is violated by the new capability step's status mapping. `if status == UNAUTHORIZED || status == FORBIDDEN { Unhealthy }` — and `Unhealthy` is the ONLY verdict that auto-disables (connection_health.rs:301-320, run_startup_health_check ~line 366). GitHub answers its anonymous primary AND secondary rate limits with **403**, and the same branch's DESIGN §1 documents this very deployment as continuously exhausting the 60-req/hour anonymous GitHub budget from a shared IP. A GitHub-kind repository probed while rate-limited therefore records `unhealthy` and is auto-disabled, even though nothing about its capability was determined. Same shape for a gated/rate-limited HF response. A rate-limit 403 is definitionally 'could not confirm', not 'credentials rejected'.

INV-4: the GitHub capability probe targets a DIFFERENT host than the repository. `capability_probe_url(Github, _) = "https://api.github.com/"`, while the repository (and the clone the download path performs) lives on `github.com`. A transport failure on that second host maps to `map_transport_error` -> `ProbeVerdict::Unhealthy` (utils.rs:717-722) -> auto-disable. So a network/proxy that reaches github.com perfectly well but blocks api.github.com now auto-disables a working repository. The probe introduced a new auto-disable trigger that is not tied to the repository's own reachability, which is precisely the 'do not disable working custom deployments' constraint the DESIGN calls out in §3.

Vacuous half of an [acceptance] test — it would still pass if the behaviour it names were reverted. `discovery_is_cached_and_degrades_honestly_when_upstream_is_gone`'s second half sets the TTL to 60s ('so the next read is forced to attempt a refresh') and then calls `take_upstream_down()`. But the cache entry is only seconds old and 60s is the CHECK-constraint FLOOR (migration 202607200500), so `get_or_refresh`'s fresh fast path (release_cache.rs:136-150) returns BEFORE `fetch` is ever invoked: the downed upstream is never contacted and the retain-on-failure branch (release_cache.rs:174, which the module docs call 'the load-bearing part') is never entered. Every assertion in that block (200, versions survive, source != unavailable, checked_at present) is satisfied by the ordinary in-TTL cache read already asserted 20 lines earlier. Reverting retain-on-failure to evict-on-failure would not turn this test red. (The branch IS covered by the in-crate unit test `failed_refresh_retains_previous_catalog`, so the behaviour is not unguarded — but no integration test proves the stale-but-labelled response ever reaches the wire.)

INV-2 partial: `get_or_refresh` has no single-flight/coalescing. The read guard is dropped before `fetch().await`, so every request that arrives after the TTL lapses issues its OWN `list_releases` upstream call before any of them writes the entry. With the discovery card mounted in several tabs/devices (and both `/versions/available` and `/{engine}/check-updates` sharing the entry, plus one entry per engine), a TTL boundary produces a burst of N GitHub requests against the same 60/hr budget the cache exists to protect. Steady state is fixed; the burst case is not, and it is unmeasured — `mock_release`'s `release_list_hits` counter would make a concurrency test trivial to write.

INV-1 latent gap: discovery and the download endpoint use two different, unshared notions of a valid backend. `parse_asset_variant` performs no character validation on the backend segment (only non-empty), while `is_valid_backend` in runtime_version/handlers.rs:67 requires `^[a-z][a-z0-9.]*$` and rejects `-`, `_` and uppercase. An asset such as `llama-server-linux-x86_64-cuda-12.9.tar.gz` or `...-CUDA12.tar.gz` would be advertised by `/versions/available` as an installable variant and then rejected with 400 INVALID_BACKEND by `/versions/download` — i.e. the 'exact set of installable combinations' promise would be false. No current trigger (every published asset is lowercase `[a-z0-9.]`), but nothing enforces that the two predicates agree.

Duplicate `#[test]` attribute on `only_a_clonable_github_origin_can_be_verified`: `#[test]` at line 944, doc comment, then `#[test]` again at line 953. rustc accepts it but emits `warning: duplicated attribute` (`duplicate_macro_attributes`). Verified by compiling the same shape in isolation. Cosmetic, but it is the signature of an attribute added without re-reading the item.

Dead test setup + an untested production path. The diff adds `LLM_REPOSITORY_GITHUB_API_BASE` to this spec's server env 'so this regression test stays offline', but the repository URL is `https://api.github.com`, which `is_clonable_github_origin` rejects — `test_repository_connectivity` returns `Unverified` at utils.rs:706-716 BEFORE `capability_probe_url` (and hence `github_api_base()`) is ever consulted. The seam is never read. Consequence: the GitHub capability branch (`capability_probe_url(Github, ..)` + `is_github_api_catalog` against a real response) has NO integration coverage anywhere in the diff — only the pure predicate is unit-tested.

Wired-and-behaving: the new discovery endpoint has no in-app consumer. `RuntimeVersion.listAvailable` appears only in the generated api-client; a grep of src-app/ui/src and tests for `listAvailable` / `versions/available` finds no call site outside generated code. The UI's AvailableVersionsCard (and the new e2e spec) still drive the surface from `/{engine}/check-updates` — the 'endpoint named for a different verb' the DESIGN §1 complains about. INV-1 is stated at the API level and IS satisfied (the route is registered in routes.rs:96 and covered by tests/llm_local_runtime/available_versions_test.rs), so this is not an invariant break — but the endpoint is production-registered and app-unconsumed, and the per-variant platform/arch data it exists to expose reaches no user surface.

AFFIRMATION (no defect): INV-3 holds in every reachable state I could find. `DownloadStatus::Completed` is written at exactly one place — `update_download_status` — and the terminal UPDATE now merges `DownloadProgressData::completed()` with the row's own stored total via a `jsonb_typeof` + range-guarded `||`, so a NULL/absent/non-numeric/<=0 total falls back to 100/100 rather than aborting. Every reader inherits it: the REST read and the SSE frame both project `progress_data` off the same row (llm_model/handlers/downloads.rs:64-85), and handlers/uploads.rs:1345 is the only production writer of the completed status. Failed/cancelled correctly keep their frozen snapshot, and `failed_download_freezes_progress_while_completed_reports_full` (tests/llm_model/download_progress_test.rs) drives BOTH terminal transitions on two identically-seeded rows through the real chokepoint with an explicit negative control — the strongest test in the diff.

AFFIRMATION (no defect): INV-1 holds and is honestly tested. `discovery_alone_yields_an_installable_five_tuple` names no tag, platform, arch or backend of its own — it reads all five out of the discovery response, POSTs them verbatim, and waits for the install to actually complete; the paired negative asserts an undiscovered tag fails with an error naming the discovery endpoint. `discovery_requires_versions_read_permission` carries a real 401 + a real 403 (a user holding `llm_local_runtime::read` but not `versions_read` — the gate is `versions_read`, permissions.rs:48) AND a 200 positive control. The `mock_release` fixture was extended with genuinely non-host assets (windows/zip, macos/metal), so the 'non-host variants are listed' assertion is not idle.
